# Vacchagotta Saṁyutta (SN 33)
**ID:** SN 33
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Vacchagotta Saṁyutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn33
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0303m.mul11.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vacchagotta Saṁyutta* (SN 33), translated as the *Linked Discourses with Vacchagotta* or *Connected Discourses with Vacchagotta*, is the thirty-third collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya* [Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral]. It consists of fifty-five brief, highly formulaic discourses recording the philosophical inquiries of the wanderer (*paribbājaka*) Vacchagotta addressed to the Buddha [Buddhism into the Year 2000; Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral]. Unusually for a section of this length, the collection is undivided into sub-chapters or *vaggas* [Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral].
The central theme across the entire *saṁyutta* is the origin of the ten speculative views or "unanswered questions" (*abyākata*) [Buddhism into the Year 2000; Bodhi 2003; Anderson 1999; Hazra 1994]. The suttas are generated through a strict permutation template: Vacchagotta asks why these views arise in the world, and the Buddha replies that they arise from not knowing, not seeing, and not comprehending each of the five aggregates (*khandha*), applying the framework of the Four Noble Truths [Bodhi 2003; Anderson 1999]. The fifty-five discourses ring permutations across the five aggregates by repeating the question and answer while cycling through eleven synonymous expressions for ignorance or lack of knowledge [Bodhi 2003]. While this collection captures Vacchagotta in his initial phase as an inquiring wanderer, later texts in the canon depict his further spiritual development, ordination, and attainment of arahantship [Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify corresponding discourses in the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ 963 and its alternate translation SĀ2 197) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus similarly confirms alignment with the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (Taishō 99) and the *Xiejian jing* (T 93), along with cross-language alignments to the Sanskrit *Mahāvyutpatti* and Tibetan canonical texts [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records widespread textual reuse with other treatments of speculative views and the aggregates, most heavily with the *Abyākata Saṁyutta* (SN 44), the *Cūḷamālukya Sutta* (MN 63), the *Dasakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10), and the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22) [DharmaNexus].

- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Samyutta Nikāya (2003) — Provides English title, structural description, analysis of the 55 permuted discourses, thematic content on aggregates and ignorance, and biographical framing of Vacchagotta.

- [Buddhism into the Year 2000] Buddhism into the Year 2000: International Conference Proceedings — Mentions that Vacchagotta-samyutta consists of fifty-five repetitive suttas on the undeclared questions.
- [Anderson 1999] Carol S. Anderson, Pain and its Ending: The Four Noble Truths in the Theravāda Buddhist Canon (1999) — Discusses how the Vacchagotta-samyutta explains that the speculative views arise out of ignorance of the body/aggregates, their arising, and their cessation.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Summarizes the saṁyutta as the wanderer Vacchagotta questioning the Buddha on the cause of speculative views.
